name: Chameleon Dermal Shift
description: Splices cuttlefish chromatophore genes into human dermal cells, allowing voluntary color-shifting across the visible spectrum. The baseline installation covers the face and hands; full-body coverage costs three times as much. Street-level clinics offer a budget version that only shifts between two or three preset colors. High-end Helix Biosystems packages include emotional reactivity — the skin changes hue in response to mood unless the user consciously overrides it. In the Shelf, mood-reactive skin is considered honest. In corporate towers, it's a liability. Most users learn to suppress the emotional bleed within a few weeks, but stress, alcohol, and strong emotion can break through the override. Children born to two chromatophore-positive parents sometimes express the trait naturally, without installation.
procedure: Retroviral dermal injection series, 3 sessions over 2 weeks
reversibility: Partially reversible with gene suppression therapy; full reversal leaves permanent mottling
side_effects: Uneven color patches if sessions are rushed
Budget versions may lock into a single color during illness
social_perception: Ubiquitous in Tiers 1–3. Fashion statements cycle through preferred palettes seasonally. Considered mundane in the Shelf, gauche if overdone in corporate settings.
story_hooks: A witness to a crime is identified by an involuntary stress-blush their skin displayed during the event
A black-market clinic's batch produces chromatophores that shift to colors outside human visual range — visible only to UV-enhanced eyes
related_entities: Arcturus Defense Solutions Thalamic Override Spike
